start_here: Say to your AI: "Put my two finished cuts first.mp4 and second.mp4 into one reel with a card before the second, and tell me where each starts." It runs the string-together step.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads the film files you name and writes one reel and an optional index text file.
instructions: 1. Clone the Workshop checkout and run brew install ffmpeg node; the reel is rendered by tools/media-composition.
2. Write reel.json: films [{file, label, card_text}], card {seconds, size, wrap_chars, line_step, colour, text_colour, border_px, noise_amplitude}, work, out, index.
3. Say "String my cuts into one reel"; the AI runs python3 tools/assemble-a-plan-into-a-cut/do-work/assemble.py string-together --request reel.json.
4. Read reel, seconds, each film's start and clock, and missing (a listed file that does not exist is named and left out); the index file lists the same starts.

worked_examples.title: Two cuts and one missing file become one reel
worked_examples.ask: Put my finished cuts into one reel with a card between them.
worked_examples.given: From test_7_string_together_puts_a_card_between_cuts in tools/assemble-a-plan-into-a-cut/test/test_assemble.py, run here: films = the same 11.1 second cut labelled first (no card) and second (card_text 'next one'), plus /no/such/file.mp4 labelled gone; card seconds 1.
worked_examples.hands_back: It printed {"result": {"reel": "<out>/reel.mp4", "seconds": 23.3, "films": [{"start": 0.0, "clock": "0:00.0", "label": "first", "seconds": 11.1}, {"start": 12.13, "clock": "0:12.1", "label": "second", "seconds": 11.1}], "missing": ["/no/such/file.mp4"]}}, and the index file holds '0:00.0  0.00s  first  (11.1s)' and '0:12.1  12.13s  second  (11.1s)'.
